newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Hortex seeks listing on foreign markets.
newsitem.headline: Polish Hortex seeks listing on foreign markets.

text.p: Polish food processor Hortex plans to enter foreign stock markets in three years, the company's board member told a news conference on Wednesday.

"With our annual turnover of $230 million, the Warsaw bourse is not our (ultimate) goal and we plan to go further. It will be legally possible for us to enter foreign stock markets within three years," Marek Tarnowski said.
Tarnowski gave no details about the company's listing on foreign exchange markets nor on the Warsaw bourse.
Hortex, which has a 37.4-percent share of the country's juice and drinks market, plans to increase it to 45 percent within the next two years.

The company's current main shareholders are the cooperative Bank Gospodarki Zywnosciowej SA (BGZ) with a 41 percent stake, Bank Handlowy with 25 percent, the Wielkopolski Bank Kredytowy with 3.5 percent and various cooperatives.

In the 12 months ending May 1997, Hortex posted sales of about 700 million zlotys and an operating profit of 45 million zlotys, compared with 561 and nine million zlotys in the similar period last year.

Within the next two months the company will be transformed into a joint-stock company, after which BGZ would hold 26 percent of the shares, the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development and Bank of America 20.5 percent each and Handlowy 15 percent.
The rest would stay in the hands of the farming cooperatives.
